text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, you should create clear and meaningful endpoints that show what each resource does. Always return the correct status codes so clients know if a request worked or failed. Good documentation is also important, because developers need to understand how to use your API without guessing. Finally, use versioning to keep your API stable. When you make big changes, a new version lets old users keep working while others move forward. Following these practices helps teams build reliable APIs that are simple to understand and grow over time.
